note: What a server answers a registration with, naming a player in the match and the seat they occupy. It shares its command value with the request it answers, which travels the other way, and it is one fixed size. Straight after a request a server sends one answer for every seat, and every one of them carries that request's build and proof back.

fields.name: clientId
fields.note: The client id the named player holds, from 0 to 252. A client whose own player this names takes it as its own.

fields.name: clientId
fields.note: The client id playerId holds. Where playerId is the client's own, the client takes this client id as its own and goes on. A watching client takes the champion of the player holding this client id as its own, so a server answers one with a client id no player in the streamed match holds (see spec/spectating.md).

fields.name: version
fields.note: The build the client said it runs. Where the answer follows a request, a server writes the number that request carried, and otherwise the build itself. A client ignores it.

fields.name: proof
fields.note: The eight bytes a request fills with its proof. Where the answer follows a request, a server writes what that request carried, and otherwise zero. A client ignores them.

fields.name: leading
fields.note: Unused; a server writes zero. It occupies the same three bytes a request uses.

fields.name: clientId
fields.note: The client id the named player holds, counted from zero. A watching client takes the champion of the player holding this client id as its own, so a server answers one with a client id no player in the streamed match holds (see spec/spectating.md).
